title: Two-affine cover separating a finite set on a curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] of topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $P\subseteq |X|$ be a finite set of closed points, and suppose that $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] on $X\setminus P$. There are affine open subschemes $U,V\subseteq X$ [def-pc-scheme] such that $X=U\cup V$, $P\subseteq V$, $U\cap P=\varnothing$, and $U\cap V$ is affine. Each of $U,V,U\cap V$ is of finite type over $k$, and both $U$ and $U\cap V$ are smooth over $k$. The empty scheme and $P=\varnothing$ are allowed.

source.place: Tag 0DZP, lemma-curve-isolated, proof, first paragraph: choice of U_2 containing the marked points and component generic points, followed by U_1 avoiding the marked points; affineness of the intersection uses separatedness.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, so every ideal is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The one-point scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the given finite-type structure morphism shows that $X$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 0DZP (lemma-curve-isolated), proof, first paragraph; Noetherian input: morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], $X$ has finitely many irreducible components. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober] each has a unique generic point; let $G$ be this finite set. The separatedness, finite-type and dimension hypotheses are exactly those of [lem-sc-dim-one-ample-invertible], which supplies an ample invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $X$. Apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-set-affine] to $P\cup G$ to obtain an affine open $V$ containing $P$ and every component generic point.

source.place: Tag 0DZP (lemma-curve-isolated), proof, first two sentences; varieties.tex Tag 0A25 (lemma-dim-1-quasi-projective), proof, ample-sheaf input; properties.tex Tag 01ZY (lemma-ample-finite-set-in-affine).

proof.text: Put $F=X\setminus V$, a closed subset. Its dimension is at most zero: otherwise it contains a strict chain $A\subsetneq B$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Since $F$ is closed these are closed in $X$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], $B$ lies in an irreducible component $C$ of $X$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], the generic point $\xi_C$ lies in $C$; step 2 placed it in $V$, hence outside $F$. Thus $B\subseteq F$ cannot equal $C$, so $B\subsetneq C$. The chain $A\subsetneq B\subsetneq C$ contradicts $\dim X\leq1$. Now [lem-sc-dim0-finite], applied to the original finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ and the closed subset $F$, shows that $F$ is a finite set of closed points.

source.place: Tag 0DZP (lemma-curve-isolated), proof, sentence "Then X minus U_2 is finite"; the dimension-zero finiteness input is the statement of lem-sc-dim0-finite.

proof.text: Because every point of the finite set $P$ is closed, $W=X\setminus P$ is open. Also $F\subseteq W$, since $P\subseteq V$. If $F=\varnothing$, take $U=\varnothing$, which is affine: the zero ring has no proper prime ideal, so its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is empty; by the definition of an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] this makes the empty open affine. If $F\ne\varnothing$, apply [lem-sc-ample-finite-principal-affine] to the ample invertible sheaf $\mathcal L$ on $X$, the finite set $E=F$, and the open $W$. It gives an affine open $U=X_s$ with $F\subseteq U\subseteq W$. In both cases $U\cap P=\varnothing$ and $X=U\cup V$, because every point outside $V$ lies in $F\subseteq U$.

source.place: Tag 0DZP (lemma-curve-isolated), proof, choice of U_1 inside the complement of the marked points; properties.tex Tag 09NV (lemma-ample-finite-set-in-principal-affine) supplies an affine neighbourhood inside the prescribed open.

proof.text: The structure map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is separated, its base is affine, and $U,V$ are affine opens. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection] makes $U\cap V$ affine. This checks separatedness over the original affine base, rather than assuming intersections affine from quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 0DZP (lemma-curve-isolated), proof, definition of U_12; schemes.tex Tag 01KP (lemma-characterize-separated), (1)(a).

proof.text: For any $T\in\{U,V,U\cap V\}$, affineness implies quasi-compactness by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. The map $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact: the affine base has just the empty and whole open subsets, whose preimages are empty and $T$. The structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Apply [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] to $T\hookrightarrow X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ to see that the open immersion $T\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact. It is of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Composing with $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and using [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) proves that each $T$ is of finite type over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0DZP (lemma-curve-isolated), proof, finite-type affine opens; morphisms.tex Tags 01T0/01T2 (finite type), 01T3 (lemma-composition-finite-type); schemes.tex Tag 01KZ (quasi-compactness in a triangle).

proof.text: The restricted structure morphism $W=X\setminus P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by hypothesis. The inclusions $U\hookrightarrow W$ and $U\cap V\hookrightarrow W$ are open immersions, because these open subsets of $X$ lie in $W$. Applying [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition] to each inclusion and the smooth morphism from $W$ proves that both $U$ and $U\cap V$ are smooth over $k$. Together with the preceding steps this proves every required clause. The argument permits empty finite sets in both affine-neighbourhood applications; in particular it applies when $P=\varnothing$ or $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0DZP (lemma-curve-isolated), proof, sentence "Then U_1 and U_12 are smooth affine schemes over k"; morphisms.tex Tags 01VC and 01VA (open immersions smooth; composition smooth).
